# Resource name_services_name_mapping

Manage a name mapping rule for an SVM. Name mapping is used to map CIFS identities to UNIX identities, Kerberos identities to UNIX identities, and UNIX identities to CIFS identities.

## Related ONTAP commands

```commandline
* vserver name-mapping create
* vserver name-mapping modify
* vserver name-mapping delete
* vserver name-mapping show
```

## Supported Platforms

* On-prem ONTAP system 9.9 or higher
* Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netapp-ontap_name_services_name_mapping" "name_services_name_mapping" {
  # required to know which system to interface with
  cx_profile_name = "cluster"
  svm_name        = "svm1"
  index           = 4
  direction       = "unix_win"
  pattern         = "test_pattern"
  replacement     = "user"
  client_match    = "10.254.101.112/28"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cx_profile_name` (String) Connection profile name
- `direction` (String) Direction of the name mapping. Possible values: krb_unix, win_unix, unix_win, s3_unix, s3_win. Cannot be changed after creation.
- `index` (Number) Position in the list of name mappings (1–2147483647). Cannot be changed after creation.
- `svm_name` (String) Name of the SVM that owns the name mapping

### Optional

- `client_match` (String) Client workstation IP address or hostname matched when searching for the pattern.
- `pattern` (String) UNIX-style regular expression used to match the name to be mapped (1–256 characters).
- `replacement` (String) Replacement name used when the pattern matches (1–256 characters).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite identifier: {svm_uuid}/{direction}/{index}

## Import

This resource supports import, which allows you to import an existing name mapping into the state of this resource.
Import requires a unique ID composed of the SVM name, direction, index, and connection profile, separated by commas.

id = `svm_name,direction,index,cx_profile_name`

### Terraform Import

For example

```shell
terraform import netapp-ontap_name_services_name_mapping.example svm1,unix_win,4,cluster
```

!> The terraform import CLI command can only import resources into the state. Importing via the CLI does not generate configuration. If you want to generate the accompanying configuration for imported resources, use the import block instead.

### Terraform Import Block

This requires Terraform 1.5 or higher, and will auto create the configuration for you.

First create the block

```terraform
import {
  to = netapp-ontap_name_services_name_mapping.example
  id = "svm1,unix_win,4,cluster"
}
```

Next run, this will auto create the configuration for you

```shell
terraform plan -generate-config-out=generated.tf
```

This will generate a file called generated.tf, which will contain the configuration for the imported resource.
